deities: Sri Panakala Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy (hilltop shrine)
Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy (foot-of-hill temple, with Lakshmi Devi on his left)
Sri Gandalaya Narasimha Swamy (hill summit shrine)
Sri Hanuman (large rock-carved relief on the hill)

history.dynasty: Vijayanagara patronage (inscriptions of Krishnadevaraya and Sadasiva Raya, 16th century); 11-storey gopuram built by Raja Vasireddy Venkatadri Nayudu, 1807-1809
history.period: Ancient (legendary origins in the Puranas); epigraphic record from the 16th century
history.summary: Mangalagiri, the 'Auspicious Hill,' is one of the eight mahakshetras of Narasimha and a three-shrine complex: the hilltop Panakala Narasimha shrine, the Lakshmi Narasimha temple at the foot of the hill, and the Gandalaya Narasimha shrine at the summit. Legend says Vishnu as Narasimha killed the demon Namuchi here and rested on the hill, which is said to be the elephant-shaped form of Hrasva Srungi; the foot-of-hill temple is traditionally attributed to Yudhishthira of the Pandavas and is mentioned in the Brahma Vaivarta Purana. Vijayanagara inscriptions record Krishnadevaraya's visit and grants under Sadasiva Raya (1538), and the striking 11-storey, 153-foot gopuram at the eastern entrance was erected by Raja Vasireddy Venkatadri Nayudu in 1807-1809. The hilltop deity has no visible idol - panakam (jaggery water with pepper, cardamom and dry ginger) is poured through a conch into the deity's open mouth, and devotees believe the lord drinks half of it, with a gurgle heard as it is accepted; in the evenings the hilltop shrine closes early as the devatas and sages are believed to worship then. The temple is administered by the Andhra Pradesh Endowments Department.

name: Sri Mangalagiri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple
town_description: Mangalagiri ('the Auspicious Hill') is a temple town in Guntur district, about 12 km from Vijayawada on the NH16 Vijayawada-Guntur highway. Besides the famous Narasimha complex on its elephant-shaped hill, the town is world-renowned for its handloom cotton saris and dress material (Mangalagiri handloom). It is a convenient day trip from Vijayawada, close to Undavalli Caves, Amaravati and the Kanaka Durga Temple.

travel.airport: Vijayawada International Airport, Gannavaram (approx. 25-32 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Mangalagiri Railway Station (approx. 2-3 km); Vijayawada Junction (approx. 15 km), well connected across India.
travel.road: On NH16 between Vijayawada (approx. 12 km) and Guntur (approx. 21 km); APSRTC buses run frequently from both cities and Amaravati. The hilltop shrine is reached by steep stone steps (constructed 1890) or by ghat road.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Narasimha Jayanti is the most spiritually significant time to visit, Brahmotsavam season the most festive.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Hilltop Panakala temple: 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM only, no evening worship (verify - one source lists closing at 4:30 PM). Foot-of-hill Lakshmi Narasimha temple: 5:00 AM to 12:30 PM and 4:00 PM to 8:30 PM. No entry fee for general darshan; panakam offering tickets available at the counter.
